figure_classifications.description: This figure shows fracture toughness as a function of test temperature for pure and K-doped tungsten, indicating brittle, semi-brittle, and ductile regimes.
This figure presents stress-strain curves for pure and K-doped tungsten at a test temperature of 20 °C, showing ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and yield strength (σ_YS).
This figure plots the ultimate tensile strength and yield strength as a function of test temperature for pure and K-doped tungsten.
This figure displays inverse pole figure maps in the normal direction, showing the crystallographic orientation and grain structure of the material.
This figure shows the brittle-ductile transition temperature as a function of the inverse square root of the grain size for pure and K-doped tungsten.
This figure illustrates the ultimate tensile strength as a function of the inverse square root of the grain size for pure and K-doped tungsten at various test temperatures.

This figure presents ultimate tensile strength and microhardness as functions of the inverse square root of grain size, and also shows the relationship between ultimate tensile strength and microhardness for pure and K-doped tungsten.

records.DBTT_definition: lower limit by the brittle data point at the highest temperature. Its upper limit is defined by the next semi-brittle data point towards higher temperatures (or ductile data point if no semi-brittle data point is present) [dbtt_methodology]
records.loading_direction_relative_to_grain: L-T crack system for SENT; along_L_direction for tensile
records.loading_rate_or_strain_rate: 1 MPa m0.5 s-1 for SENT; 10-3 s-1 for tensile
records.notes: Confirmed: can read Fig.1 (fracture toughness vs. test temp), Fig.2 (stress-strain curves), Fig.3 (UTS/YS vs. test temp), Fig.4 (EBSD map), Fig.5 (DBTT vs. grain size), Fig.6 (UTS vs. grain size), Fig.7 (UTS/HV vs. grain size). Also read Supplementary Tables S1, S2, S3, S4. Table 1 mentioned in text but not provided. [grain_size_methodology] Grain size (d_ND(HAB)) estimated from Fig.5a. [grain_boundary_area_to_volume_per_um] Calculated as 1/d_ND due to single direction grain size. [dbtt_methodology] DBTT determined as temperature range between highest brittle data point and next semi-brittle/ductile data point. [fracture_toughness_caveat] Fracture toughness (K_Q) values are geometry-dependent and overestimated, not K_IC, due to EDM notch and thin samples. [hardness_methodology] Hardness value estimated from Fig.7a. [tensile_methodology] UTS, YS, total elongation estimated from Fig.2a and text. Tensile tests also performed at 300, 400, 600, 800 °C (Fig.3) but only 20 °C data extracted. [processing_caveat] This material represents an intermediate stage in the rolling process and may not be a standard commercial material.

[finding] High DBTT and brittle behavior attributed to 'orientation bands' in microstructure.
